title: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Instrumental Variables (IV) estimation with agroecological suitability (z) as an instrument for new seed variety adoption (x). The key assumptions are: (1) Relevance - agroecological suitability is correlated with seed adoption decisions, (2) Exclusion restriction - agroecological suitability affects farm income only through its effect on seed adoption, and (3) Exogeneity - agroecological suitability is uncorrelated with unobserved factors affecting farm income.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s79_data.csv")

# Display basic statistics
cat("Dataset Summary:\n")
summary(data)
cat("\nCorrelations:\n")
cor(data)

# First stage: Check instrument relevance
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== FIRST STAGE RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Coefficient on instrument (z):", round(coef(first_stage)["z"], 4), "\n")
cat("F-statistic for weak instruments test:", round(summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1], 2), "\n")

# Check if F-stat > 10 (rule of thumb for strong instrument)
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
if(f_stat > 10) {
  cat("Instrument appears strong (F > 10)\n")
} else {
  cat("Warning: Weak instrument (F < 10)\n")
}

# Second stage: IV estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)

cat("\n=== IV RESULTS (SECOND STAGE) ===\n")
iv_summary <- summary(iv_model)
print(iv_summary)

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
cat("\nKey Result - Causal Effect of Seed Adoption on Farm Income:\n")
cat("Coefficient:", round(iv_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(iv_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(iv_coef - 1.96*iv_se, 4), ",", round(iv_coef + 1.96*iv_se, 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. OLS for comparison (biased but useful benchmark)
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_coef <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
cat("OLS coefficient (likely biased):", round(ols_coef, 4), "\n")

# 2. Reduced form (effect of instrument on outcome)
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
cat("Reduced form coefficient:", round(rf_coef, 4), "\n")

# 3. Manual IV calculation (should match ivreg)
manual_iv <- rf_coef / coef(first_stage)["z"]
cat("Manual IV calculation:", round(manual_iv, 4), "\n")

# 4. Test overidentifying restrictions (would need more instruments)
cat("Note: Exact identification - cannot test overidentifying restrictions\n")

# 5. Endogeneity test
endogeneity_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("Wu-Hausman test p-value:", round(endogeneity_test$diagnostics["Wu-Hausman", "p-value"], 4), "\n")

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("The causal effect of new seed variety adoption on farm income is:", round(iv_coef, 4), "\n")
if(iv_coef > 0) {
  cat("This suggests that seed adoption INCREASES farm income.\n")
} else {
  cat("This suggests that seed adoption DECREASES farm income.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient (approximately 0.3-0.8) indicating that new seed variety adoption increases farm income. The effect should be economically meaningful since improved seed varieties typically enhance productivity through better yields, disease resistance, or drought tolerance. The IV estimate may differ from OLS due to selection bias - farmers who adopt new varieties may have unobserved characteristics (like management skills) that independently affect income, making IV estimation crucial for causal identification.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use agroecological suitability as an instrument for new seed variety adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Adopting the new seed variety leads to a significant increase in farm income.
